ai.description: *Nasikabatrachus bhupathi* is a stout, 5–6 cm frog with a dark purple body and a pale snout. It features a pointed head, tiny eyes, and specialized limbs for subterranean life.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nasikabatrachus bhupathi* is best distinguished from *N. sahyadrensis* by its distinctively pale, creamy-white snout and venter compared to the latter's darker coloration.
ai.habitat: *Nasikabatrachus bhupathi* inhabits the eastern slopes of the southern Western Ghats, specifically residing in moist deciduous forests at elevations around 250–300 meters.
ai.behavior: *Nasikabatrachus bhupathi* spends most of its life underground, emerging only briefly during monsoon rains to breed in temporary pools.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nasikabatrachus bhupathi* breeds during the pre-monsoon rains, laying eggs in flowing forest streams. Females deposit clutches of approximately 3,000 eggs in rock pools.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nasikabatrachus bhupathi* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu, India, specifically inhabiting the Srivilliputhur-Megamalai landscape at mid-elevations.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Nasikabatrachus bhupathi* is a low-pitched, pulsed, sheep-like bleat emitted by males while calling from underground burrows during monsoon rains.
